title: BCA/11/2022 of SWAMI GOPALANANDA GIRI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Bail Cancellation Application No. 11 of 2022
Swami Gopalananda Giri ........Applicant
Versus

Present:-
Mr. Rajendra Arya, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Akshay Latwal, Brief Holder for the State.
Mr. Gaurav Singh, Advocate for the respondent no. 2.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The applicant seeks cancellation of order dated
05.01.2022 passed in Bail Application No. 18 of 2022,
whereby the respondent no. 2 has been granted bail in
Case Crime/FIR No. 683 of 2021, under Sections 408 and
420 IPC, registered at P.S. Kotwali Haridwar, District
Haridwar.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. The respondent no. 2 was granted bail in Case
Crime/FIR No. 683 of 2021, under Sections 408 and 420
IPC, registered at P.S. Kotwali Haridwar, District Haridwar,
on 05.01.2022 in Bail Application No. 18 of 2022. On that
date, on behalf of the informant, a statement was given
that "if the accused is ready not to withdraw any

2
amount regarding the FDRs, as alleged in the FIR, his
bail application may be considered".
4. Now, bail cancellation application has been filed
on the ground that the respondent no. 2 has withdrawn
money from the FDRs.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit
that after the bail order dated 05.01.2022, the respondent
no. 2 has withdrawn money from the FDRs.
6. Learned counsel for the respondent no. 2 would
submit that FDRs of Rs. 20 lakh was prepared by the
respondent no. 2, which is still intact in the bank. He
would submit that after bail order, the respondent no. 8
has not withdrawn any amount.
7. Learned State Counsel would submit that prior
to bail order, money was withdrawn by the respondent no.
2, but thereafter he did not withdraw any amount from the
bank account.
8. The basis on which the bail cancellation
application has been filed has no ground. The State as well
as the respondent no. 2 has categorically stated that no
money was withdrawn from the FDRs. Nothing otherwise
has been shown by the applicant. Therefore, there is no

3
ground to cancel the bail of the respondent no. 2.
Accordingly, the bail cancellation application deserves to
be dismissed.
9. The bail cancellation application is dismissed.
